PUBLIC COMMENTS
The public is encouraged to address the City Council or any of its Agencies listed on this agenda on any matter posted on the agenda or on any other matter within its jurisdiction. If you wish to address the City Council or any of its Agencies, you may do so during the PUBLIC COMMUNICATIONS period noted on the agenda. Each person is allowed three (3) minutes speaking time. A Spanish speaking interpreter is available for your convenience.
COMENTARIOS DEL PUBLICO
Se invita al público a dirigirse al Concilio o cualquiera otra de sus Agencias nombradas en esta agenda, para hablar sobre cualquier asunto publicado en la agenda o cualquier tema que esté bajo su jurisdicción. Si usted desea la oportunidad de dirigirse al Concilio o alguna de sus Agencias, podrá hacerlo durante el período de Comentarios del Público (Public Communications) anunciado en la agenda. A cada persona se le permite hablar por tres (3) minutos. Hay un intérprete para su conveniencia.
Any written public record relating to an agenda item for an open session of a regular meeting of the City Council that is distributed to the City Council less than 72 hours prior to that meeting will be available for public inspection at City Hall in the City Clerk's office at 14403 E. Pacific Avenue, 3rd Floor during normal business hours (Monday - Thursday, 7:30 a.m. - 6:00 p.m.)

MINUTES
  BALDWIN PARK CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING
  May 1, 2019, 7: 00 P. M.
  COUNCIL CHAMBER - 14403 E. Pacific Avenue, Baldwin Park, 91706

These minutes  are presented  in Agenda order.  Various announcements or discussions
may have occurred before or after the title under which they are presented.
CALL TO ORDER

The meeting was called to order by Mayor Lozano at 7: 07 p. m.

INVOCATION

The invocation was provided by Pastor Jackson.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Mayor Lozano.

ROLL CALL

MEMBERS PRESENT:
Council Member Alejandra Avila
Council Member Paul C. Hernandez
Mayor Pro Tern Monica Garcia
Mayor Manuel Lozano

MEMBERS ABSENT:
Council Member Ricardo Pacheco

MOTION: It was moved by Mayor Lozano, seconded by Council Member Avila to excuse
Council Member Pacheco from the meeting. Motion carried by unanimous consent.
REPORT ON CLOSED SESSION

Mayor Lozano announced direction was provided to staff to continue the recruitment for
the position of Chief of Police until filled. Direction was provided by unanimous consent.
ANNOUNCEMENTS

MOTION: It was moved by Mayor Lozano, seconded by Mayor Pro Tern Garcia to add
Subsequent Need Item A- 1 to the agenda and accept corrections to the Special Meeting
Minutes included in Item No. 2. Motion carried by unanimous consent.

City Clerk Ayala explained  the  corrections  made  to the Special  Meeting minutes  of April
  17, 2019 included in Item No. 2.

 Mayor Lozano invited everyone  to attend  the Cinco de Mayo  4th
  Boxing Show on May
 and  the  Community Input Meeting of May 16th.

 PROCLAMATIONS, COMMENDATIONS &  PRESENTATIONS
  Proclamation for Lupus Awareness Month

The proclamation was introduced by Mayor Pro Tem Garcia and was presented to Estella
 Mata an advocate for all Lupus patients who thanked the City Council for the
acknowledgement.

  Proclamation for Older Americans Month/ Certificates

The proclamation was introduced by Mayor Pro Tem Garcia and was presented to
seniors involved in teaching various classes.

  Proclamation for National Bicycle Month

The proclamation was introduced by Council Member Hernandez and was presented to
  Proclamation for Mental Health Awareness

The proclamation was introduced by Mayor Lozano and was presented to Diana Rivera
Beltran  Educational  Outreach  Program  Coordinator  at  Kaiser. Ms.  Rivera  Beltran
commended the students from Sierra Vista High School for their hard work in raising
awareness amongst students and reducing stigma and suicide rates.

Diana Aguilar student at Sierra Vista High provided an overview of their program to raise
awareness.

  Plaque Recognition to Lieutenant Mark Adams for his Years of Service with the
  City of Baldwin Park Police Department

The plaque was presented by Mayor Lozano. The City Council thanked Lieutenant Adams
for his years of service to the community.

Lieutenant Adams said it was a pleasure to serve this community and stated the city
would hold a special place in his heart.

PUBLIC COMMUNICATIONS
Mayor Lozano opened Public Communications at 7: 38 p. m. and noted that each speaker
was permitted a total of three ( 3) minutes to speak.

Donna Camou, retired teacher of Baldwin Park Unified School District spoke in opposition
of the proposed Planned Parenthood clinic.

Regular Meeting of 05/ 1/ 19  Page 2 of 6
 Mr. Rios questioned  the qualification  requirements  applied to the position of Chief of
Police and expressed safety concerns on the construction of curbs around the city.

Eduardo Sauceda welcomed the newly appointed Chief of Police and requested City
Council' s assistance in helping the homeless and veterans.

Mr. Luna expressed  concerns  with the current appointment  of Chief of Police and
questioned the actions taken by the Mayor and Council Member' s during the dismissal of
former personnel appointed to serve in that capacity.

Mayor Lozano closed public communications at 7: 54 p. m.

Mayor Lozano commented on the achievements of a few individuals who have previously
served in the Baldwin Park Police Department.

Council  Member  Avila  thanked  Lieutenant  Adams  for his service  and  updated  the
community on the safety message relayed by staff to contractors working throughout the
city. Council Member Avila thanked the residents for expressing their concerns and
extended an invitation to schedule a meeting with any Council Member for those wishing
to further discuss any matter.

Mayor Lozano directed the public to visit our website for more information  on Measure H
and provided an apology to Interim Chief of Police Patino for the lack of introduction.

Mayor Pro Tem Garcia also thanked  Lieutenant Adams for his service and addressed
comments made regarding independent decisions made by each Council Member in
relation to previous employee appointments/ dismissals.

Mayor Lozano commented on false propaganda perpetuated by a group.

CONSENT CALENDAR
All items listed under the consent calendar are considered to be routine business by the
Council Members and were approved with one motion.

MOTION: It was moved by Mayor Pro Tern Garcia, seconded by Council Member Avila
to table Item No. 5 from the Consent Calendar. Motion carried by unanimous consent.

MOTION: It was moved by Mayor Lozano, seconded by Council Member Hernandez to
table Item No. 4 from the Consent Calendar. Motion carried by unanimous consent.

MOTION:  It was moved by Mayor Lozano, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Garcia to
approve the Consent Calendar including the corrections to Item No. 2 and the addition of
Subsequent  Need Item No. A- 1 and with the exception of Item No.' s 4 and 5. Motion
carried by unanimous consent.

Regular  Meeting of 05/ 1/ 19  Page 3 of 6
 1. Warrants and Demands
  The City Council ratified the attached Warrants and Demands Register.

2. Meeting Minutes
  The City Council received and filed the following Meeting Minutes:
  A. Meeting Minutes of the Special City Council Meetings held on April 17, 2019

  corrected meeting minutes were approved).
  B.  Meeting Minutes of the Regular City Council Meetings held on April 17, 2019.

3. Rejection of Claims
  The City Council rejected the following claim( s) and directed staff to send appropriate
  notice of rejection  to claimant( s):

  Farias, Adrian  The claimant is alleging injury to hand while
  driving a Foothill Transit bus.

  Monterosa, Jessica Cristina  The claimant is alleging property damage to
  her vehicle.

  First Group America aso Joyce  The claimant alleges dangerous  condition  of
  Clark  public property.

4. Approval of Use Agreement with the County of Los Angeles for Construction and
  Maintenance of the San Gabriel River Class 1 Commuter Bikeway in Exchange
  for the use of County Right- of-Way ( Pulled from the Consent Calendar)
  This item was not considered.

5. Renewal  of  Grant  Writing Services Contract with  California  Consulting,  LLC
  Pulled from the Consent Calendar)
  This item was not considered.

6. Consideration  of  a  Disposition  and  Development  Agreement  with  MG

  13057- 13065 Garvey Avenue
  The City Council provided direction in regards to a Disposition and Development
  Agreement ( DDA) with MG Development; and authorized the City Manager to execute
  the agreement after a final review by the City Attorney; and approved Resolution No.
  2019- 017, entitled " A Resolution of the City Council of the City of Baldwin Park

  Approving a Disposition and Development Agreement Between the City of Baldwin
  Park  and  MG  Development  Group, LLC ( aka  MG  Development)  For a Proposed
  Industrial Development Project at 13057- 13065 Garvey Avenue."

7. Ratify and Adopt a Resolution to Amend the City of Baldwin Park Comprehensive
  Pay Schedule in Accordance with CaIPERS established Guidelines
  The City Council approved, ratified and adopted Resolution No. 2019- 018 amending
  the City of Baldwin Park Comprehensive Pay Schedule, retroactive to April 17, 2019.

 A- 1. Subsequent Need Item
  Adopt Resolution No. 2019- 019, " A Resolution  of the City Council of the City of
  Baldwin Park, California, Adopting the Fiscal Year 2019-20 Project List to be
  Funded  by Senate Bill 1 ( SB1) — the Road Repair and Accountability Act"
  The  City Council adopted Resolution No. 2019- 019, " A Resolution of the City Council
  of the City of Baldwin Park, California, Adopting the Fiscal Year 2019- 20 Project List
  to be Funded by Senate Bill 1 ( SB1) — the  Road Repair and Accountability Act".

REPORTS OF OFFICERS
8. Review  of  Commission  Applicants  and  Consideration  of

  Appointments/ Reappointments to Fill the Scheduled Vacancies for the Housing,
  Planning and Recreation Commissions

  MOTION:  It was moved by Mayor Lozano, seconded by Mayor Pro Tern Garcia to
  bring this item back for Council' s consideration in June. Motion carried by unanimous
  consent.

CITY  COUNCIL /  CITY  CLERK /  CITY  TREASURER /  STAFF  REQUESTS &
COMMUNICATIONS

None

Mayor Lozano requested an update on cleanup efforts made by the 99 cent store parking
lot owners.

Director of Community Development Benjamin Martinez stated staff had made contact
and would report back at a later time.

Mayor Lozano additionally requested staff alert street vendors, particularly on the Frazier
exit ( corner  of  Main and Merced), of the new regulations and inform them that a permit is
required.

Council Member Avila inquired whether a warning would be issued and requested staff
report back on Hollywood Housing to assist in affordable housing/ transitional housing via
a presentation.

Mayor Lozano confirmed a warning would be issued.

Council  Member  Hernandez  recognized  recreation  staff  for  hosting  past  events

successfully, such as the Itsy Bitsy Soccer team awards, Easter Egg hunt Celebration,
and the Tree Ceremony where leaders were honored.

  ADJOURNMENT
 There being no other business to discuss, and all other matters having been addressed,
a motion was made by Mayor Lozano, seconded by Mayor Pro Tern Garcia, to adjourn
the meeting at 8: 09 p. m.
